headline: Vocab Radar Activity - Instant Vocabulary Confidence Map
outcomes: Students rate how well they know key words before the lesson moves into practice
Teachers see which vocabulary needs support and which words the class can already use
The activity makes vocabulary knowledge visible without embarrassing individual students
Students become more aware of their own word confidence before reading, listening, or discussion
howItWorks: LessonCaptain selects five or six key words connected to the class topic
Students rate each word from unfamiliar to confident on their own device
The teacher screen shows a live vocabulary map of class confidence
The teacher chooses which words to teach, skip, or recycle later in the lesson
teacherUseCases: Pre-teaching vocabulary before a video, article, or listening task
Checking which words are worth spending class time on instead of guessing
Starting a topic lesson with student self-assessment rather than a teacher lecture

faq.a: No. It is a confidence check. Students are not marked right or wrong; they report how familiar each word feels so the teacher can make better decisions.
Vocab Radar can generate words from your topic, and it works especially well inside a full lesson where the source or topic already defines the language focus.

faq.q: Why ask students to rate words before teaching?
faq.a: It prevents wasted time. If the class already knows several words, you can move faster. If a key word is unfamiliar to most students, you can pause before the main task breaks down.

faq.q: How do students rate each vocabulary item?
faq.a: No. Students join through the live lesson link and respond without signing in.
